# @forgesworn/shamir-core

> GF(256) Shamir's Secret Sharing for TypeScript. Zero runtime dependencies.

Full reference with more examples and implementation notes: llms-full.txt (shipped in this package, also at https://github.com/forgesworn/shamir-core/blob/main/llms-full.txt).

## What It Does

Splits a secret (any Uint8Array) into n shares where any threshold-sized subset can reconstruct the original. Uses Shamir's Secret Sharing over GF(256) with Lagrange interpolation.

## Install

npm install @forgesworn/shamir-core

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 19, or any runtime with a global crypto.getRandomValues (browsers, Deno, Bun). splitSecret uses the global crypto directly. On Node.js 18 it throws a ReferenceError unless Node is started with --experimental-global-webcrypto (workaround, not supported). reconstructSecret does not use crypto.
- ESM only. require('@forgesworn/shamir-core') fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED because the exports map has only an import condition. From CommonJS use `await import('@forgesworn/shamir-core')` inside an async function.

## Imports

All exports are named exports of the package entry point. There is no default export.

```typescript
import {
  splitSecret,
  reconstructSecret,
  ShamirError,
  ShamirValidationError,
  ShamirCryptoError,
  type ShamirShare, // type only
} from '@forgesworn/shamir-core';
```

## API

### splitSecret(secret: Uint8Array, threshold: number, shares: number): ShamirShare[]

Split a secret into shares. threshold must be in [2, 255]. shares must be in [threshold, 255].

```typescript
import { splitSecret } from '@forgesworn/shamir-core';
const shares = splitSecret(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]), 2, 3);
// shares[0] = { id: 1, threshold: 2, data: Uint8Array }
```

### reconstructSecret(shares: ShamirShare[], threshold: number): Uint8Array

Reconstruct from at least threshold shares. Uses first threshold shares only; later entries are neither used nor validated.

```typescript
import { splitSecret, reconstructSecret } from '@forgesworn/shamir-core';
const shares = splitSecret(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]), 2, 3);
const secret = reconstructSecret(shares.filter((s) => s.id !== 2), 2);
// secret = Uint8Array [1, 2, 3]
```

### ShamirShare

```typescript
interface ShamirShare {
  id: number;        // 1-255 (GF(256) evaluation point)
  threshold: number; // 2-255 (minimum shares to reconstruct)
  data: Uint8Array;  // same length as original secret
}
```

The maths uses only id and data. reconstructSecret checks threshold against its threshold argument only when the share's threshold is an integer; a missing or non-integer value skips the check.

### Errors

- ShamirError (base, never thrown directly)
- ShamirValidationError extends ShamirError (bad inputs; the only class the public functions currently throw)
- ShamirCryptoError extends ShamirError (internal GF(256) zero-inverse guard; unreachable through the public API with current validation)

splitSecret throws ShamirValidationError when: secret is not a Uint8Array or is empty; threshold or shares is not a safe integer; threshold is outside 2-255; shares is below threshold or above 255.

reconstructSecret throws ShamirValidationError when, among the first threshold entries: the threshold argument is not an integer >= 2; shares is not an array or has fewer than threshold entries; an entry is not an object; an id is not an integer in 1-255 (id 0 is rejected); data is not a Uint8Array; two ids are equal; an integer threshold on a share differs from the argument; the first entry's data is empty; data lengths differ.

If crypto.getRandomValues is missing, splitSecret throws the runtime's own error, not a Shamir error.

## Key Properties

- Zero runtime dependencies (only Web Crypto for randomness)
- GF(256) with log/exp table lookup (same irreducible polynomial as AES: 0x11b)
- Internal polynomial coefficients and random bytes zeroed after use; the caller's secret, the returned shares and the reconstructed secret are not zeroed by the library
- Share IDs are 1-indexed (1-255), not 0-indexed
- No secret length limit
- Threshold metadata on shares is validated during reconstruction when present as an integer
- Node.js >= 19, browsers, Deno, Bun

## Security Notes

- No integrity check: a wrong, corrupted or mixed-up share returns wrong bytes without an error. Verify the result at application level.
- Not constant-time: table lookups are indexed by secret-dependent bytes and multiplication returns early on zero operands.
- No fallback randomness: only crypto.getRandomValues.

## Related Packages

- @forgesworn/shamir-words: BIP-39 word encoding for shares
- dominion-protocol: epoch-based encrypted access control
